match.reason: The closest card, mat-gradient-as-rate-change, covers only straight-line gradients, but this point also covers curved graphs of real data (temperature, motion, containers of different shapes), and the derivative cards are beyond Units 1 and 2 depth.

draft.title: Rates in context
card: On a graph of real data, the gradient is a rate. Its units are the vertical units per horizontal unit, such as km per hour or °C per hour.
A steeper graph means a faster rate of change. A flat section means no change at that time, such as a cyclist who has stopped.
A line that slopes up means the quantity is increasing. A line that slopes down means it is decreasing.
Water filling a container at a steady rate: the depth rises quickly where the container is narrow and slowly where it is wide. A container with straight sides of the same width gives a straight line.
draft.remember: Read the gradient as a rate. Steeper means faster, flat means no change.

a.q: A graph of a cyclist's distance (km) against time (hours) is steepest between 2 and 3 hours. What does this show?
opts: She rode the furthest in total
She had stopped for a rest
a.why: On a distance and time graph, the steepest part has the greatest distance per hour, so the fastest speed. A flat part would be a rest, not a steep one.
a.clue: Steep means a lot of distance in a short time.

b.q: A vase fills with water at a steady rate. The graph of depth against time rises steeply at first, then gets gradually less steep all the way to the top. Which vase fits?
opts: Narrow at the bottom, getting wider towards the top
Wide at the bottom, getting narrower towards the top
The same width all the way up
Wide in the middle, narrow at the bottom and top
b.why: Depth rises fastest where the vase is narrow, so the vase starts narrow. The graph keeps flattening, so it keeps getting wider. A vase wide at the bottom would fill slowly at first, which is the reverse.
b.clue: Steep depth graph means the water level is climbing quickly.

b.best: Narrow at the bottom, getting wider towards the top
